mappings.indicator_name: Lack of dedicated legal framework for cybersecurity
mappings.verbatim_quote:
A person commits an offence if:
(a) the person engages in conduct; and
(b) the conduct has the result that an article or thing, or software,
becomes vulnerable:
(i) to misuse or impairment; or
(ii) to being accessed or modified by a person not entitled to
access or modify it; and
(c) the article or thing, or software, is or is part of public
infrastructure; and
(d) the person engages in the conduct with the intention that
prejudice to Australia’s national security will occur (whether
at the time or at a future time).
mappings.impact: A person commits an offence if they engage in conduct that makes public infrastructure vulnerable to misuse, impairment, or unauthorized access, with the intention of causing prejudice to Australia’s national security.

mappings.indicator_name: Lack of dedicated legal framework for cybersecurity
mappings.verbatim_quote:
A person commits an offence if:
(a) the person deals with information or an article; and
(b) the person intends that the person’s conduct will prejudice
Australia’s national security; and
(c) the conduct results or will result in the information or article
being communicated or made available to a foreign principal
or a person acting on behalf of a foreign principal.
mappings.impact: A person commits an offence if they deal with information or an article with the intention that their conduct will prejudice Australia’s national security and the conduct results or will result in the information or article being communicated or made available to a foreign principal or a person acting on behalf of a foreign principal.

mappings.indicator_name: Lack of dedicated legal framework for cybersecurity
mappings.verbatim_quote:
(1) It is a defence to a prosecution for an offence by a person against
this Subdivision that the person dealt with the information or
article:
(a) in accordance with a law of the Commonwealth; or
mappings.impact: The provision allows a defence for a person who dealt with information or an article in accordance with a law of the Commonwealth, which implies that such actions are permitted under existing Commonwealth law, including potentially cybersecurity-related laws.

mappings.indicator_name: Lack of dedicated legal framework for cybersecurity
mappings.verbatim_quote:
(1) In this Part:
cause harm to Australia’s interests means to:
(a) interfere with or prejudice the prevention, detection,
investigation, prosecution or punishment of a criminal
offence against a law of the Commonwealth; or
(b) interfere with or prejudice the performance of functions of
the Australian Federal Police under:
(i) paragraph 8(1)(be) of the Australian Federal Police Act
1979 (protective and custodial functions); or
(ii) the Proceeds of Crime Act 2002; or
(c) harm or prejudice Australia’s international relations in
relation to information that was communicated in confidence:
(i) by, or on behalf of, the government of a foreign country,
an authority of the government of a foreign country or
an international organisation; and
(ii) to the Government of the Commonwealth, to an
authority of the Commonwealth, or to a person
receiving the communication on behalf of the
Commonwealth or an authority of the Commonwealth;
or
(f) harm or prejudice the health or safety of the Australian public
or a section of the Australian public; or
(g) harm or prejudice the security or defence of Australia.
mappings.impact: The provision defines 'cause harm to Australia’s interests' to include harm or prejudice to the security or defence of Australia, which establishes a legal basis for protecting national security information, including through the classification and handling of sensitive data.

mappings.indicator_name: Lack of dedicated legal framework for cybersecurity
mappings.verbatim_quote:
A person commits an offence if:
(a) the person communicates information; and
(b) the information is inherently harmful information; and
(c) the information was made or obtained by that person by
reason of his or her being, or having been, a Commonwealth
officer or otherwise engaged to perform work for a
Commonwealth entity.
mappings.impact: The provision prohibits a person from communicating inherently harmful information obtained due to their role as a Commonwealth officer or someone engaged to perform work for a Commonwealth entity, with penalties including up to 7 years in prison.

mappings.indicator_name: Lack of dedicated legal framework for cybersecurity
mappings.verbatim_quote:
(1) A person commits an offence if:
(a) the person communicates information; and
(b) either:
(i) the communication causes harm to Australia’s interests;
or
(ii) the communication will or is likely to cause harm to
Australia’s interests; and
(c) the information was made or obtained by that person by
reason of his or her being, or having been, a Commonwealth
officer or otherwise engaged to perform work for a
Commonwealth entity.
mappings.impact: Prohibits Commonwealth officers or persons engaged to perform work for a Commonwealth entity from communicating information that causes or is likely to cause harm to Australia’s interests.

mappings.indicator_name: Requirements to allow Government access to personal data

An AFP member may apply to an issuing authority for an initial
preventative detention order in relation to a person.
mappings.impact: An AFP member may apply to an issuing authority for an initial preventative detention order without requiring a court decision or judicial warrant.

mappings.indicator_name: Requirements to allow Government access to personal data
mappings.verbatim_quote:
If an initial preventative detention order is in force in relation to a
person in relation to a terrorist act, an AFP member may apply to
an issuing authority in relation to continued preventative detention
orders for a continued preventative detention order in relation to
the person in relation to the terrorist act.
mappings.impact: An AFP member may apply to an issuing authority for a continued preventative detention order without needing a court order or judicial warrant, allowing government access to personal data related to a person under detention.

mappings.indicator_name: Requirements to allow Government access to personal data
mappings.verbatim_quote:
The AFP Minister, or a legal representative of the AFP Minister,
(the applicant) may apply to a Supreme Court of a State or
Territory for either of the following:
(a) a continuing detention order in relation to a terrorist offender;
(b) an extended supervision order in relation to a terrorist
offender.
mappings.impact: The AFP Minister may apply to a Supreme Court for a continuing detention order or an extended supervision order in relation to a terrorist offender, and the Court may make such an order if satisfied that the offender poses an unacceptable risk of committing a serious Part 5.3 or 5.3A offence.
